reflections.summary: Lost Game 3 and series 1-2 in 7 turns with 0 piloting errors - loss was preview/strategy, not execution. Preview plan backfired: Farigiraf/Sylveon/Kingambit/Staraptor (staraptite) into Delphox-Mega/Sinistcha/Incineroar had no Heat Wave resist and relied on Helping Hand + Pixilate Hyper Voice to bypass Rage Powder. T1 Helping Hand + Hyper Voice into Sinistcha Protect gifted Delphox a free Nasty Plot (+2 to 69% HP) then +2 Psyshock OHKO'd Sylveon, and boosted Heat Wave spread controlled the game. Trick Room war also backfired: cancelling their T2 Trick Room with our own Trick Room removed our speed control, then re-setting TR T4 kept the game under TR where boosted Heat Wave could spread KO Staraptor (T5) and OHKO Kingambit (T6) despite Rage Powder/Protect. Mega choice was wrong: we never Mega Evolved Staraptor (no Contrary value) while opponent correctly Mega Evolved Delphox T1 and swept with it.
reflections.adjustment: In a future series vs this Delphox-Mega/Sinistcha core do not bring Sylveon/Staraptor or Helping Hand into Protect to enable Nasty Plot. Bring a Fire resist/Heat Wave switch-in and single-target pressure that punishes Protect/Nasty Plot turns, and either deny Trick Room with pressure/Taunt or commit to it - do not cancel their TR with your own. If bringing Staraptite must Mega Evolve immediately for Contrary Close Combat value, otherwise bring a different Mega/answer that resists Fire/Psychic and can ignore Rage Powder without relying on spread.

reflections.summary: Won game 3 and the series 2-1 because the between-game adjustment worked exactly as designed: Mega Delphox took +2 SpA via Nasty Plot on turn 1 behind Sinistcha's Protect, comfortably tanking the Helping Hand Hyper Voice (resisted, 70%), then OHKO'd Sylveon with Psyshock while Sinistcha's Trick Room cancelled Farigiraf's, stripping their speed control. From there the Rage Powder + spread-Heat-Wave pattern was airtight: Kingambit's Sucker Punch failed into the redirector, +2 Heat Wave removed Staraptor from full and guaranteed-OHKO'd Kingambit, and Incineroar — the Psychic-immune endgame answer — finished Farigiraf with a super-effective Throat Chop once its Protect chain failed. Piloting was clean (0 decision errors, 7 turns). Team-preview assessment: the four brought (Delphox/Sinistcha/Incineroar/Sneasler) and the Delphoxite Mega choice suited this opponent perfectly — Delphox resists their Fairy/Psychic core, Sinistcha is the hard answer to Farigiraf's TR, Incineroar blanks Farigiraf, and Sneasler covered the Arcanine-H/Kingambit line they ultimately didn't exploit. The opponent adapted between games (new Sylveon TR-mode lead) but not within the game, repeating failed Sucker Punches and Protect-spam into predicted Heat Wave turns.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the same core plan — it is now series-proven — but expect the next adaptation: they already swapped from Raichu+Farigiraf (G1/G2) to Farigiraf+Sylveon TR mode (G3), so a future series may open with Kingambit or Arcanine-H to pressure Delphox before it sets up. Against that, keep Sneasler ready (Close Combat answers both, 4x SE into Kingambit), never let Kingambit target Delphox without Rage Powder active (LO Sucker Punch KOs from ~70%), and never switch Incineroar in while Kingambit lives (Defiant). Preserve Sinistcha better — it was sacked to Kowtow Cleave at 68%; consider Protecting it on predicted Kowtow turns so the TR reversal survives deeper into the game. Continue punishing their Protect-spam habit by doubling into the Protect-reduced slot, exactly as the turn-7 Throat Chop on Farigiraf closed it.
